samples: It is a reusable retry helper: given an action that takes no arguments and either succeeds with a result or fails, plus a maximum number of attempts, it runs the action up to that many times and returns the first successful result. After each failure, whatever its kind, it remembers the error as text and sleeps for a delay that starts at 100 ms and doubles every time, plus a random extra of up to a quarter of the base delay, and it sleeps this way even after the final failure. If every attempt fails it fails with a gave-up error carrying the attempt count and only the last error's text, and using it means accepting a delay schedule that cannot be configured or capped, declaring the time and random capabilities, and using an error type that can be converted to text.
